cells.tense: You are at the desk where the pattern has just closed and the pen is still in your hand.
cells.act: take the turning as it comes
cells.ask: Before you tidy the finished thing or start sketching the next one, give it a minute of being finished. Notice whatever is already arriving — a question, a small pull — and let that, rather than your plan, decide what comes next.
cells.core: You can build a frame that holds a mess and still let the frame end. When a cycle closes, you know it closed, and you don't need to bolt the next one on before the ink dries. The structure was for getting through, not for keeping. You're at the edge of one of these now, and the pull to start the next shape is already there. That pull isn't wrong — it's just early. The piece you finished is allowed a minute of being finished. When the minute is up, what comes next will show itself, and you won't have had to invent it. Standing in the open where the last structure ended and the next hasn't started is the whole position. Receive what's arriving instead of reaching for it.
cells.sheetLine: A cycle can close and stay closed for a minute.
cells.verb: gathering what has been lived into a whole that can be released
cells.place: the desk where scattered pieces get made into a frame others can build inside

cells.tense: You will have written the ending before the last chapter has finished happening.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Pick the thing you're driving toward finishing and hold it open three more days. Each time the urge to call it done shows up, note what is still moving, and leave that moving.
cells.core: Where you put things into workable shape, you keep arriving early — deciding how it lands before the landing has happened. The frame goes up before you know the load, so you call the cycle complete while what's underneath it is still in motion. Out there it passes for decisiveness; in here it means nothing gets its own arc. The closed thing gets reopened anyway, usually by events. Try meeting the material where it actually is. Three days is long enough to feel the difference between a thing being done and a thing you've decided is done. What arrives by itself has a shape you didn't have to impose. Let the door open at the hour it opens, not before.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that had already closed behind you and you were still waiting.
cells.act: open the door to the next thing on time, not early
cells.ask: Take something still sitting in your pending pile, held open past its own end. Put today's date beside it and mark it closed. Then close one small loop: send the message, put the box away, stop the search.
cells.core: There's a frame near you that has gone without a final line. Something ended — or plainly didn't — and you kept it in the pending pile, and the pending pile has been quietly running your days. You're still at a threshold that moved. Not knowing which cycles have closed isn't a flaw in you; it's a missing line, and lines can be drawn. You don't have to feel finished first. You can put the pen down, and the feeling will arrive later, and you can set the whole thing down either way. Pick the smallest loop and close it today. The next thing is already waiting behind that door, and it has been waiting on your hand, more than on your readiness.

cells.tense: The frame is being drawn and the hand doing it does not look up from the paper.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: For a spell, don't touch the frame you keep — whatever shape it holds other people in. Don't fix it, don't explain it. When you reach for it, stop. Later, see what still stands without you.
cells.core: You keep something in working shape — a plan, a rhythm, a piece of order other people live inside — and if asked, you'd say you weren't doing anything in particular. The structure is yours. What's wanted here isn't more building; it's knowing what you already built and whether it needs you in it. So try setting it down. Not discarding it — putting it down deliberately and watching whether it holds. Some of what you're gripping is a completed thing you haven't let yourself hand over. Release here isn't defeat and it isn't the end of your usefulness. It's the difference between the frame you made and the frame you are. Empty hands will tell you which is which, faster than thinking about it.

attempts.check: Unsupported: I render Authority's pattern-work as something the person is actively doing in the Unacknowledged cell (a frame being maintained while the person says they are not) — the record gives the capacity and the shadow, not evidence that others have noticed or relied on it. Reader's objection: 'I'm not running anyone's structure; I genuinely don't know if anything closed' — the cell must survive that as a live possibility, so the ask is framed as putting the pen down and noticing, which works whether or not a frame exists. The ask survives being wrong: the six Source acts and the Faith act are usable regardless of the read. The sentence serving me more than the person: 'you are the turning' — it sounds like praise and would rather flatter the writer than hand anything over; cut it from the cores.
